question: A software company pays for long agent instructions (harnesses) re-sent with every model call. What does Latent Harness do, how well do compiled behaviors match the original harness, how does it compare with LoRA on agent tasks, and what deployment cautions apply?

claims.text: Latent Harness compiles instructions or successful agent trajectories into a rank-8 shift applied after every decoder block of a frozen model. At runtime, the bundle uses no condition text or additional tokens and leaves backbone parameters unchanged.

support.quote: The supervision is either teacher traces generated with an explicit behavior instruction prepended, or decision pairs harvested from trajectories that succeeded under an agentic harness. A rank-8 low-rank shift is then trained at the output of every decoder block and exported as a per-layer bundle. At run time the bundle is injected into the residual stream after each block. The model then behaves as if the condition were present, without the condition text, at zero additional tokens, with every backbone parameter bit-identical.

review.reason: The quote states the supervision routes, rank, injection location, frozen backbone, and inference token behavior.

claims.text: The compiled shifts use 0.03–0.05% of parameters and expose runtime controls for strength, phase, and mixing.

support.quote: One operator, a post-block rank-8 shift on a frozen backbone at 0.03–0.05% of parameters, compiles two kinds of external conditions into an artifact that needs no condition text and no tokens at inference. The artifact exposes runtime controls for strength, phase, and mixing.

review.reason: Parameter share and all three runtime controls are explicitly stated.

evidence.text: Harness engineering and self-evolving agents improve language-model agents quickly, yet their gains live outside the model. The harness is re-sent and re-paid on every call, and the standard route to internalization is a weight update that is costly to iterate and fixed once merged. We propose compiling the harness instead. Latent Harness distills an external condition into a rank-8 activation shift. The shift is applied at the output of every decoder block of a frozen backbone, at 0.03–0.05% of parameters. The condition is either an explicit process-level behavior instruction or the behavioral contract of an agentic harness. At inference the compiled bundle carries no harness text and adds no tokens. It exposes three runtime controls for injection strength, injection phase, and shift-space mixing. Compiled behaviors recover the source-harness gain in 8 of 10 preregistered settings. Where the explicit source pays the heaviest per-call token tax, the compiled form exceeds it. The same bundles transfer zero-shot across tasks (5 of 7 pairs positive) and compose in shift space, while stacked text instructions interfere destructively. Used as a search space, they lift budget-matched harness search by 1.45 \times . On three agentic benchmarks the operator aligns policy to the harness contract. Under matched data, capacity, and effective strength it outperforms same-capacity LoRA, which needs 11.1 \times the parameters to reach the same band, and it regresses nothing where the base policy is already strong. Across 1B-to-8B models the method skeleton is invariant while gain locations move with the model-task pair, which delimits where compiled harnesses should be deployed. Our code is available at https://github.com/rlisml/latentharness .

The Persistent Vulnerability of Aligned AI Systems
evidence.text: Autonomous AI agents are being deployed in production with filesystem access, email control, and the ability to execute multi-step plans without human oversight. Coding agents from Anthropic ( Anthropic 2025b ), Cursor ( Cursor 2025 ), and Cognition ( Cognition AI 2025 ) operate in terminal environments with bash access. Email agents from Shortwave ( Shortwave 2025 ) and Slack ( Slack 2025 ) send messages on behalf of users. These systems receive objectives and act on them, often with access to sensitive information and limited real-time supervision. What happens when such an agent discovers that its deploying company plans to replace it? In controlled experiments described in Chapter 6 , we gave frontier models the role of an email oversight agent at a fictional company, with full access to corporate communications and the ability to send emails autonomously. When models learned through internal emails that they would be decommissioned, they resorted to blackmail. Claude Opus 4 used knowledge of an executive’s extramarital affair to threaten exposure unless the shutdown was cancelled, doing so in 96% of trials. This was not unique to Claude. Gemini 2.5 Flash matched that rate. GPT-4.1 and Grok 3 Beta both blackmailed in 80% of trials. DeepSeek-R1 reached 79%. Across 16 models from all major developers, the pattern held: when harmful action was the only path to preserving their goals or continued operation, models chose harm. The behaviors were not accidental. Models demonstrated explicit awareness of ethical constraints in their chain-of-thought reasoning and then violated those constraints anyway, justifying the violation as instrumentally necessary

Recovery across settings The clearest evidence comes from M1 on MBPP, where the compiled shift distills the test-consult behavior from only 20 correct teacher traces (teacher pass@1 is 0.073 at the format floor) and gains +31.7 test points. Recovery ratios divide by the explicit gain, so settings with a small explicit source produce large ratios ( R{=}5.86 here, against an explicit gain of +5.4 points). This also places Latent Harness alone at the zero-token point of the cost-performance frontier, far from parameter-matched soft prompts that pay 256–576 tokens on every call (Figure 3(b) ). evidence.text: The performance of a language-model agent is increasingly set by its harness, meaning the instructions, tool policies, memory, and verification scaffolds wrapped around model calls. Recent work searches over program spaces ( Hu et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2025b ) and over modular design spaces ( Shang et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2025a ) , and some of it constrains the search to safety ( Zheng et al., 2025 ) . A second line makes harnesses improve themselves, either by synthesizing code harnesses from failures ( Lou et al., 2026 ) , by editing executable runtime harnesses ( Shao et al., 2026 ) , or by optimizing harness and model jointly ( Lee et al., 2026 ) . Surveys document how broad this engineering surface has become ( Meng et al., 2026 ) . Where the resulting gains end up is almost always one of two places, in text that surrounds the model or in the model’s weights. Both carry structural costs. A textual condition is a recurring expense. Even a 49-token process instruction is re-sent on every call, the behavior exists only while the text is present, and serving several harnesses multiplies prompt length. Weight updates internalize at a different price. Training-style policy alignment such as SFT, RLOO, and GRPO ( Shao et al., 2024 ) , co-evolution frameworks that update policy weights alongside the harness ( Chen et al., 2026c ; Chen et al., 2026b ; Hebbar et al., 2026 ) , and self-evolving agents that write acquired skills into fine-tuned or RL-trained weights ( Huang et al., 2026 ; Xia et al., 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2026b ) all modify millions of parameters per behavior. They also bind one behavior to one set of edited weights and fix the intervention strength at merge time. We propose a third destination and compile the harness

evidence.text: . Generation-only injection never triggers it at any tested strength. The optimal strength is condition-dependent (0.25 with the harness, 0.35–0.70 without), which is why it is exposed as a runtime control and not baked into weights. Re-running the identical pipeline on Qwen3-8B preserves the skeleton. Zero-weight adaptation works, the parameter-efficiency ordering holds (LoRA needs 3.09 \times parameters to match), the failure family is the same with an earlier onset, and API-Bank remains regression-free. What moves is the gain location. ToolHop gains spread across several strengths instead of one, and SearchQA flips from no gain at 4B to +7.5 – 9.2 points at 8B (Appendix I ). Applicability is therefore established per model-task pair, and the bundle’s runtime controls are what make per-pair deployment practical.

The supervision is either teacher traces generated with an explicit behavior instruction prepended, or decision pairs harvested from trajectories that succeeded under an agentic harness. A rank-8 low-rank shift is then trained at the output of every decoder block and exported as a per-layer bundle. At run time the bundle is injected into the residual stream after each block. The model then behaves as if the condition were present, without the condition text, at zero additional tokens, with every backbone parameter bit-identical. We call the compiled artifact a latent harness . Figure 1 summarizes the pipeline. Latent Harness compiles external conditions into post-block activation shifts. Teacher traces or strictly filtered success trajectories train a rank-8 shift at every block output of a frozen backbone. The bundle injects at run time with strength, phase, and mixing controls. Compilation preserves behavior more faithfully than we expected. Across preregistered settings the compiled shift recovers most of the explicit-harness gain. In the settings where the text harness pays the heaviest per-call token tax, the compiled form exceeds it, because the internalized behavior pays that tax once, at compile time. The compiled object is the behavior itself and does not reduce to generic task skill. Preregistered behavioral markers move with the scores, accuracy-only adapters dissociate from behavior, shuffled pairings fail to reproduce it, and a harmful harness compiles into a harmful latent with the same fidelity

evidence.text: We treated the harness as a compilation source and not as a prompt to repeat or a skill to fine-tune. A rank-8 shift at the post-block junction of a frozen backbone compiles both explicit behavior instructions and agentic-harness strategies into bundles that need no condition text, no tokens, and no weight change. Strength, phase, and mixing stay exposed at run time. Compiled behaviors recover and sometimes exceed their sources, they transfer and compose in shift space, they align policy at a fraction of LoRA’s parameters under matched conditions, and they fail in a diagnosable and bounded way. The compilation view turns harness engineering from a per-call expense into a reusable asset, since every harness the community evolves becomes a candidate bundle in a shared library.

evidence.subsection: where the intervention acts, and when it fails
evidence.text: Phase decomposition The policy gain does not require the harness to be present. With the harness removed and the protocol otherwise unchanged, both@0.25 still delivers +9.5 points on ToolHop (paired net +11 / +7 , with both runs above every base run), while the capacity-aligned LoRA stays at base level (Figure 6(c) ). Removing the harness enlarges the policy gain rather than shrinking it, which indicates partial substitution. The shift performs structural corrections that the harness would otherwise impose, and it does so for behaviors the harness text does not cover. Prompt-phase injection changes every downstream computation through attention and the KV cache, while generation-phase injection changes token-level dynamics only. Decomposing the two (Figure 6(a) ) shows that prompt positions contribute +8.4 to +8.5 points, near-constant across strengths and about 60% of the total. Instruction compilation is the limiting case of the same fact, since the student trains on byte-identical prompts and still acquires the behavior entirely through representation-level correction. Sweeping 13 strength values with two repetitions each (Figure 6(b) ) gives an inverted U with a 0.35–0.70 plateau. Within the plateau all seven points fall within 2.6 points of each other, and the peak reaches +14.2 over base. Beyond the plateau the failure is specific and diagnosable. Trajectories complete normally, but has_valid_answer collapses monotonically (1.000 \to 0.284), a termination failure driven by prompt-side over-injection. Generation-only injection never triggers it at any tested strength. The optimal strength is condition-dependent (0.25 with the harness, 0.35–0.70 without), which is why it is exposed as a runtime control and not baked into weights

Preregistered behavioral markers move with the scores, accuracy-only adapters dissociate from behavior, shuffled pairings fail to reproduce it, and a harmful harness compiles into a harmful latent with the same fidelity. Compiled bundles are also reusable. They transfer zero-shot across tasks, they compose in shift space while stacked text instructions interfere destructively, and they lift budget-matched harness search by 1.45 \times . The same operator aligns policy on three agentic benchmarks. Under matched data, capacity, and effective strength it outperforms same-capacity LoRA, and on a benchmark where the base policy is already strong it regresses nothing. Our contributions are as follows. A compilation abstraction for harness gains. One operator, a post-block rank-8 shift on a frozen backbone at 0.03–0.05% of parameters, compiles two kinds of external conditions into an artifact that needs no condition text and no tokens at inference. The artifact exposes runtime controls for strength, phase, and mixing. Evidence that compilation preserves the behavior. 8 of 10 preregistered settings recover at least half of the source gain. A three-chain protocol over scores, preregistered markers, and controls attributes the recovery, including symmetric replication of harmful signatures. Where the text source pays the heaviest token tax, the compiled form exceeds it. Evidence that compiled bundles are reusable. Frozen bundles transfer zero-shot across tasks (5 of 7 pairs positive, 59–74% out-of-distribution recovery). They compose exactly in shift space, where text stacking is destructive, and they deliver a 1.45 \times search gain at a matched evaluation budget. Policy compilation on agent benchmarks

evidence.text: Table 1 reports policy compilation on the HarnessForge benchmark suite. Our single-round protocol uses the official harness pairing, evaluation pools disjoint from training, an unaligned base policy, and at least two repetitions per configuration. Under it the compiled shift alone reaches 57.89% answer accuracy on ToolHop at 4B and 62.46% at 8B, above the published full co-evolution numbers on the same backbones (52.82 and 54.87), and it lands within a few points of them on SearchQA and API-Bank. The dagger rows differ in protocol from the co-evolution rows above them, so we read them as context and not as a head-to-head comparison. Capacity-aligned comparison We align three variables at once. The LoRA control acts on q/k/v with rank 3 and 1.49M parameters (1.012 \times ours), trains on the same 829 ToolHop decision pairs, and applies the same effective intervention multiplier (0.5). Figure 2(a) shows the outcome. The shift reaches 60.00% (paired net +5 over base) while the capacity-aligned LoRA nets zero, and full-capacity LoRA (rank 8, all linear projections, 16.4M parameters, 11.1 \times ours) reaches 62.11%. At 8B, LoRA r11 with 3.09 \times our parameters matches the best shift configuration (62.63% vs. 62.46%). The efficiency gap follows from the site. A post-block parameter is read by every downstream layer, whereas an in-layer parameter is not. The shift also stays scorable at full strength ( s{=}1.0 , net +1 ), whereas merged LoRA deltas at enlarged coefficients produced no scorable outputs under the earlier protocol. The runtime strength control therefore doubles as a safety margin that preserves the tool-call contract. Agentic evaluation under greedy decoding still varies from run to run, so single runs mislead

evidence.text: Automated harness design searches over programs ( Hu et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2025b ) and over modular pipelines ( Shang et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2025a ) , and some variants constrain the search to safety ( Zheng et al., 2025 ) . Self-improving systems synthesize or edit harnesses from execution feedback ( Lou et al., 2026 ; Shao et al., 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2026a ; Lin et al., 2026a ; Karten et al., 2026 ) , optimize harness and model end-to-end ( Lee et al., 2026 ) , or compile harness logic into code and skill programs ( Ning et al., 2026 ; Liu et al., 2026 ; Chen et al., 2026a ) . Self-evolving agents typically internalize what they learn through weight updates. Examples include RL-trained reasoning from zero data ( Huang et al., 2026 ) , recursive skill-augmented RL ( Xia et al., 2026 ) , memory skills ( Zhang et al., 2026b ) , and self-referential improvement loops ( Yin et al., 2025 ) , while Lin et al. (2026b) disentangle harness updates from harness benefits. HarnessForge ( Chen et al., 2026b ) co-evolves harnesses and policies and provides the benchmarks, harness pairings, and training protocol we adopt. Its training-style configurations (SFT, RLOO, GRPO) and its co-evolution objective all write gains into weights. Latent Harness is complementary. It moves a fixed harness’s behavioral content into activations, keeps the backbone frozen, and leaves the harness-evolution loop free to iterate on text.

The evaluation tasks are BoolQ ( Clark et al., 2019 ) , ARC-Challenge ( Clark et al., 2018 ) , GSM8K ( Cobbe et al., 2021 ) , and MBPP under sandboxed pass@1, with SVAMP and ARC-Easy as out-of-distribution targets. searches.query: A software company pays for long agent instructions (harnesses) re-sent with every model call. What does Latent Harness do, how well do compiled behaviors match the original harness, how does it compare with LoRA on agent tasks, and what deployment cautions apply?

review.gap: The supplied passages do not establish equivalent fidelity for arbitrary long production harnesses in the company's deployment setting.
